name: Adaptation
description: Reduced neural response to sustained or repeated stimulation. Allows the nervous system to adjust sensitivity based on stimulus history. Mechanisms include synaptic depression, calcium-dependent inactivation, and intrinsic membrane properties.
key_references: Webster, M. A. (2011). Adaptation and visual coding. Journal of Vision, 11(5), 1-23.
Abbott, L. F., Varela, J. A., Sen, K., & Nelson, S. B. (1997). Synaptic depression and cortical gain control. Science, 275(5297), 220-224.
empirical_evidence: Ubiquitous across sensory systems with multiple timescales (ms to hours). Early-stage adaptation involves synaptic mechanisms; longer timescales involve gene expression. Explains contrast sensitivity, texture perception, and stimulus selectivity. Functionally important for detecting changes in the environment.
